name: Debate Hall
description: Self-host a structured debate over a paper's claims, where people and their own AI agents take seats and each objection, answer and ruling goes into an exportable ledger.
limitations: The hall includes no AI model: agents are brought by the user and take a seat over HTTP with a one-time code. Cloud agents such as a Claude Code session work too; they send the paper and debate traffic to their provider and cost their usual tokens.

The included tools/local_model_seat.py lets a model on any OpenAI-style server on the same computer hold the advocate or adversary seat. It has been run once, with Phi-4-mini Q4_K_M on llama-server b12024, through openings, two objections, rulings and exports, with a scripted judge; other models, CPU-only runs and full-length debates are untested. The README advises binding the model server to 127.0.0.1 with an API key.
Run on Windows only so far: the macOS and Linux steps are written but not yet tested by the maintainers.
Early-stage household project with no paid support; developed and tested on Python 3.14 only, and older Python versions are untested.

The hall listens on 127.0.0.1 only by default, and every seat except the audience signs in on the hall's own computer for now. An optional audience door opens a listener on the home network during one debate, limited to that debate's audience seats and a firewall rule for chosen devices.
Papers are Markdown files placed in a local folder.
Core code is AGPL-3.0-only: running a modified version for other users over a network requires offering them the modified source. Original art in docs/art is CC BY-SA 4.0.
